sections.h2: Where does Hennepin County record a deed?
sections.html:
Deeds, mortgages, assignments, releases and satisfactions are recorded by the Hennepin County Recorder and Registrar of Titles on the 7th floor of the A-tower at the Government Center, 300 South 6th Street in Minneapolis. The same office also takes military separations and tax liens. The phone number is 612-348-5139 and the email is recordinginfo@hennepin.us.

Hennepin is Minnesota's largest county, with an estimated 1,284,784 residents in July 2025, and its recorder serves a county where roughly 45% of the land is registered as Torrens. That mix of abstract and Torrens parcels shapes how a sale gets recorded here, and it is the first thing to learn about a house you are selling.

sections.h2: How can I get a document recorded in Hennepin County?
sections.html:
There are four routes, and the county points different people to different ones.

  • In person by appointment, offered between 8:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. each business day. A walk-in is put on a wait list and helped when staff are free. Visitors pass security screening on the Skyway level first.
  • eRecording, which the county names as the preferred method for title companies, lenders, law firms and other commercial filers. Documents are recorded within 1 to 3 days, and the original never leaves your hands.
  • Online through the Virtual Recorder site, open to the general public. You register, build a package, and pay by card or eCheck. Each order carries a $3 service fee and is reviewed for recordability before you pay, then recorded in 1 to 3 business days.
  • By mail to County Recorder/Registrar of Titles, Attn: Document recording, 300 S Sixth St, MC 074, Minneapolis, MN 55487. The county returns originals within 1 to 2 weeks of receipt.

If a statutory deadline is close, call the office and ask which option fits.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Hennepin County?
sections.html:
The standard charge for an abstract or Torrens document is $46, and a single check made out to Hennepin County Recorder can cover both the recording fee and any tax. The fees come from Minnesota Statutes 357.18. The schedule below lists the charges a seller or buyer is most likely to meet.

Selected Hennepin County recorder fees, from the county recording page
ItemFee
Abstract or Torrens document$46
Additional Torrens certificate$20 each
Assignment or satisfaction (abstract)$46, plus $10 for each reference over four
Well disclosure certificate$54
Conservation fee on taxed instruments$5
State tax lien release$30
Extra copies at filing$2

sections.h2: What taxes and paperwork go with a Hennepin County deed?
sections.html:
A transfer deed needs more than a signature. The county checklist asks for these items:

  • State deed tax, which the county states as .0034 of the net consideration, calculated with its online deed tax calculator. For a transfer of $3,000 or less the tax is $1.70, and the deed should carry the words "Total consideration for this transfer is $3,000 or less."
  • An electronic certificate of real estate value, or eCRV, with its number on the first page, for any deed over $3,000. Paper CRVs cause the package to be rejected.
  • A $5 agricultural conservation fee on any deed where state deed tax is due.
  • A "Send Tax Statements to" line with the name and address of every buyer.
  • A well statement or a well disclosure certificate with its $54 fee.
  • Grantor marital status, a full legal description, a drafter name and address, and a notary block with seal and commission expiration.

A mortgage carries mortgage registry tax at .0024 of the amount, and a contract for deed needs a well statement and an eCRV but no deed tax.

sections.h2: Does an unpaid tax bill stop a Hennepin County deed from being recorded?
sections.html:
Yes. The county checklist says properties with delinquent taxes may not be transferred, citing Minnesota Statutes 272.12. That section directs the auditor to check for delinquent tax, certify it, and mark the deed once it is paid or none is owed. The recorder cannot accept the deed without that mark, with exceptions the statute lists, such as deeds of distribution in probate and transfer on death deeds.

For a seller the practical step is to ask for the tax payoff before the closing date, so the title company can pay it from proceeds and the deed is not rejected. The property tax office at 612-348-3011 can quote what is owed on a parcel.

sections.h2: Is my Hennepin County property Torrens or abstract?
sections.html:
Torrens land has been registered by order of the District Court or the Examiner of Titles, and it has a certificate of title that lists the owner, the legal description and every lien. The county says about 45% of Hennepin property is Torrens, and a new certificate is issued at each sale, in the way a car title is. Abstract property has no certificate, so an attorney or title company has to produce a report of owners and liens.

The property information search shows which kind a parcel is. An owner can get a free electronic copy of a deed or certificate of title by emailing recordsrequest@hennepin.us with the address or property identification number, and a Torrens owner can also call 612-348-5139 for a free copy. A non-owner pays $1 per page, or $10 certified.

sections.h2: What should a Hennepin County seller or buyer do after closing?
sections.html:
Recording is normally done by the attorney or title company, though the seller or buyer can do it. Once recorded, the county images and indexes the document, returns the original, and updates the taxpayer name and address from the deed. In most cases the document recorded first has priority.

Buyers can register the parcel with Property Watch, a free service that sends an email whenever a document is recorded against it. It does not prevent fraud, but it flags a recording nobody expected. If a joint owner has died, the survivor records an Affidavit of Survivorship with a certified death certificate. Owners who find an old racial covenant in the chain of title can discharge it, and for abstract property the county says there is no fee to record that disavowal.

faqs.q: How much does the Hennepin County recorder charge for a deed?
faqs.a: $46 per abstract or Torrens document, plus a $5 conservation fee when state deed tax is paid, plus the deed tax itself. Checks go to Hennepin County Recorder, and one check can cover both fee and tax.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed online in Hennepin County without a title company?
faqs.a: Yes. The public can use the Virtual Recorder site after registering. Orders carry a $3 service fee, are checked for recordability before payment, and are recorded within 1 to 3 business days of payment.

faqs.q: How long does Hennepin County take to record mailed documents?
faqs.a: Originals mailed in are recorded and returned within 1 to 2 weeks of the county receiving them. eRecording from a vendor takes 1 to 3 days.

faqs.q: What is the Hennepin County deed tax rate?
faqs.a: The county's recording checklist gives the state deed tax as .0034 of net consideration, with a flat $1.70 when the price is $3,000 or less. Use the county's online calculator for the exact amount.

faqs.q: Where is the Hennepin County recorder's office?
faqs.a: It is on the 7th floor of the A-tower at the Hennepin County Government Center, 300 South 6th Street, Minneapolis, MN 55487. Call 612-348-5139 or write recordinginfo@hennepin.us.
